Primo
PREE-moh
adjective (Boomer slang)
From Italian and Spanish primo, "first" (Latin primus). As American slang for first-rate, top-quality, the best of its kind, primo spread in the 1970s, partly through Spanish-speaking communities in the Southwest and California and partly through the drug trade, where primo marked the best-grade marijuana; it soon broadened to anything excellent ("primo seats," "a primo wave").

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Primo means first-rate, top-shelf, the best available: primo seats at the ballgame, a primo parking spot, a primo surf break. The word is literally "first." The Christian observation: Scripture has a great deal to say about what comes first, and it reorders our list. "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you" (Mat 6:33). The primo thing in a believer’s life is not a seat or a parking spot but the reign of God. Christ Himself is the true Primo: "he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence" (Col 1:18), and He says, "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last" (Rev 22:13). Israel was taught to give God the primo portion of everything: "The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the LORD thy God" (Exo 23:19); "Honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase" (Pro 3:9). The habit the word suggests — grabbing the best for oneself — is the habit Scripture reverses: the best goes to God first, and the Christian takes the lower seat at the feast. Teach a child to give God the primo, and to let others have the primo seat.

Webster 1828 Definition

Boomer-era slang (1970s, from Spanish / Italian primo, "first") for top-quality, first-rate — a word Scripture turns toward the One who must have the preeminence (Col 1:18) and the firstfruits given to God (Pro 3:9).

expand to see more

PRIMO, adj. (American slang, 1970s–present) First-rate, top-quality, excellent. "We got primo seats." Originally also of high-grade marijuana.

Webster (1828) — PRIME, adjective [Latin primus.] 1. First in order of time; original; as prime fathers; prime creation. In this sense, the use of the word is nearly superseded by primitive, except in the phrase, prime cost. 2. First in rank, degree or dignity; as prime minister. 3. First in excellence; as prime wheat; cloth of a prime quality. Humility and resignation are prime virtues.

Decode for families: in a teenager’s mouth today it is usually innocent; in a 1970s context it may refer to drugs.

Modern Corruption

Primo trains the eye to grab the best for oneself; Scripture gives the first and best to God and teaches the believer to take the lower seat.

expand to see more

The word is harmless, but the instinct behind it deserves a look. Primo is about getting the best — the best seat, spot, grade, deal. Our Lord watched guests at a feast doing exactly that, choosing the chief rooms, and told them to take the lowest place instead, "For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased." The Christian does not despise good things; he simply does not grab them.

The deeper reordering is in worship. Israel’s firstfruits law meant that the first sheaf, the first lamb, the first coin belonged to God before anything belonged to the family. That is not stinginess about the rest; it is a confession about who comes first. A household that gives God the primo portion — of its income, its week, its attention — is living Mat 6:33 in the most concrete way.

Latin primus (first) → Italian / Spanish primo → 1970s American slang primo (first-rate).
